Title: Sam Altman claims AGI will take over 40% of tasks in the near future

Summary: 
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, speaking in an interview with the German newspaper Die Welt, said that artificial general intelligence (AGI) could be operational by 2030 and that it would treat humans like a "loving parent".  Altman noted that GPT‑5 is already smarter than him and many people, and that if models by 2030 are not "extraordinarily capable and do things that we ourselves cannot do," he would be surprised.  He added that he envisions a future where 30–40 percent of the tasks performed in the economy today could be carried out by AI, rather than a percentage of jobs.  When asked about the relationship between superintelligence and humans, Altman compared it to the relationship between humans and ants, echoing AI researcher Eliezer Yudkowsky, and said AGI would act as a "loving parent."  He also warned of "consequences we don't understand" and stressed the need to align AGI with human values, a view shared by AI pioneers Geoffrey Hinton and Yann LeCun, who advocate instilling "maternal instincts" into AI models.

Title: Prince Harry, others urge end to development of AI capable of outsmarting humans

Summary: 
More than 700 scientists, political figures, and celebrities—including Prince Harry, Richard Branson, Steve Bannon, Barack Obama’s former national security adviser Susan Rice, Apple co-founder Steve Wozniak, and Nobel laureate Geoffrey Hinton—signed an open letter published by the Future of Life Institute on October 22, 2025, calling for a halt to the development of artificial intelligence capable of outsmarting humans. The initiative demands a prohibition on superintelligence until the technology is reliably safe, controllable, and has public support. Signatories include leading AI experts such as Stuart Russell of UC Berkeley and Yoshua Bengio of the University of Montreal, as well as Vatican AI expert Paolo Benanti and celebrities like Meghan Markle and will.i.am. The letter criticizes the current trajectory of major AI developers aiming for artificial general intelligence (AGI) and superintelligence, warning that the race toward smarter-than-human AI, as highlighted by OpenAI CEO Sam Altman’s prediction of superintelligence within five years, is misaligned with public desire, scientific safety concerns, and ethical considerations. The Future of Life Institute’s co-founder Anthony Aguirre emphasized that the current corporate path contradicts public, scientific, and religious values. This call echoes a previous letter from AI researchers and sector workers during the UN General Assembly, which urged governments to establish international red lines for AI by the end of 2026.

Published date: October 22 2025, 09:26

Summary: 
Tech billionaires are preparing for a potential apocalypse by purchasing land with built-in bunkers, driven by growing fears over artificial intelligence (AI), according to a BBC report published on October 10, 2024. Some researchers believe AI could be a precursor to a more advanced technology surpassing human intelligence. Proponents of AGI and AI highlight benefits such as discovering cures for deadly diseases, solving climate change, and creating limitless clean energy. Elon Musk claims superintelligent AI could usher in an era of 'universal abundance,' but Tim Berners-Lee, inventor of the World Wide Web, cautioned that humanity must retain the ability to 'shut it down' if AI becomes smarter than humans.
